papers.title: A TPMS-based method for modeling porous scaffolds for bionic bone tissue engineering
papers.abstract: In the field of bone defect repair, gradient porous scaffolds have received increased attention because they provide a better environment for promoting tissue regeneration. In this study, we propose an effective method to generate bionic porous scaffolds based on the TPMS (triply periodic minimal surface) and SF (sigmoid function) methods. First, cortical bone morphological features (e.g., pore size and distribution) were determined for several regions of a rabbit femoral bone by analyzing CT-scans. A finite element method was used to evaluate the mechanical properties of the bone at these respective areas. These results were used to place different TPMS substructures into one scaffold domain with smooth transitions. The geometrical parameters of the scaffolds were optimized to match the elastic properties of a human bone. With this proposed method, a functional gradient porous scaffold could be designed and produced by an additive manufacturing method.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种基于TPMS的梯度多孔支架设计方法，并优化了弹性模量匹配，但缺乏LPBF制造和疲劳测试。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), or surface roughness characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 设计仿生梯度多孔支架以匹配骨力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用TPMS和S型函数建模，有限元优化弹性模量。
summary_zh.result: 实现了功能梯度多孔支架的可控设计。
summary_zh.validation: 通过兔股骨CT数据验证有限元结果。

summary_en.motivation: To design gradient porous scaffolds that mimic bone morphology and mechanical properties.
summary_en.method: A modeling method using TPMS and sigmoid function to create smooth transitions and optimize elastic properties via FEM.
summary_en.result: The method enables the design of functional gradient porous scaffolds suitable for additive manufacturing.
summary_en.validation: Finite element simulations validated against CT-derived morphological data from rabbit femoral bone.
